1. INTRODUCTION
1.1 Purpose of this Report
This report presents ERA’s review of the Uganda Electricity Supply
Industry (ESI) Main Grid Tariffs for the third quarter of 2025 (July –
September 2025). It outlines the tariff review outcomes and the
corresponding revenue requirement approvals, which formed the
basis for determining the approved end-user tariffs for the period.
1.2 Background
Following the takeover by Uganda Electricity Distribution Company
Limited (UEDCL) of the concession formerly operated by Umeme
Limited in April 2025, the Authority, at its 424th Meeting, considered
and approved a revised 2025 Base Tariff. This decision was informed
by:
a)The consolidated operations of UEDCL;
b)The approved Tariff Performance Parameters for UEDCL;
c) Umeme Limited’s Buyout Amount;
d)The consolidation of energy sales and customer numbers; and
e) The rollout of tariff initiatives to customers in the former UEDCL
concession areas.
The review of the third-quarter tariffs for 2025 was conducted with
reference to the following:
a) The Uganda Electricity Distribution Company Limited
(UEDCL)’s Licences for Distribution and Sale of Electricity;
b)The Uganda Electricity Generation Company Limited
(UEGCL)’s Licence for Generation and Sale of Electricity for
the Nalubaale and Kiira Hydropower Stations;
c) The Bulk Power Supply Licence issued to Uganda Electricity
Transmission Company Limited (UETCL), and;
d)The Quarterly Tariff Adjustment Methodology, 2014.

For the purpose of determining the Capacity Price for Nalubaale
and Kiira Hydropower Stations, the Bulk Supply Tariff for UETCL, and
the Distribution Price for UEDCL, the Authority considered changes
in; the Consumer Price Index, the exchange rate of the Uganda
Shilling (USh) against the United States Dollar (USD), fuel prices on
the international market, and the energy generation mix. This led to
adjustments for:
a) Inflation Rate, resulting in the Inflationary Adjustment Factor
(IRAF);
b) Exchange Rate, resulting in the Foreign Exchange Rate
Adjustment Factor (FERAF);
c) International Fuel Prices, resulting in the Fuel Price Adjustment
Factor (FPAF), and;
d) Energy Mix and other Authority-approved costs, resulting in
the Energy Mix Adjustment Factor (EMAF).
1.3 Major Assumptions for the Third Quarter 2025 Tariff Review
The third quarter Tariff Review was based on the following major
factors/assumptions:
a) Licences for the Distribution and Sale of Electricity issued to
UEDCL. The Licence for Sale of Electricity provides the Tariff
Methodology guiding the determination of retail tariffs
effective April 2025.
b) Consolidation of UEDCL’s operations with the distribution
concession area formerly operated by Umeme Limited,
covering regulatory targets, customer numbers, energy sales
per customer category, tariff reduction initiatives, billing, and
the applicable tariff structure.

3.1.2 Country’s Economic Performance and Growth
The Bank of Uganda maintained the Central Bank Rate (CBR) at
9.75% in its May 2025 Monetary Policy Statement. This decision aims
to safeguard price stability, support sustainable economic growth,
and keep inflation expectations below the 5% medium-term target.
Uganda’s economy continues to strengthen, with GDP growth in
the first half of FY 2024/25 recorded at 6.0%. This reflects an
improvement over the same period in FY 2023/24, though slightly
below the 6.6% growth achieved in the second half of that year.
Growth has been driven primarily by a recovery in household
spending, supported by rising real incomes.
For the full FY 2024/25, overall GDP growth is projected at 6.0% –
6.5%, with prospects of reaching 7.0%. This outlook is underpinned
by stronger agricultural and industrial production, increased
investment in the extractives sector, and continued
implementation of government initiatives such as the PDM.
3.2 GENERATION ASSUMPTIONS
3.2.1 International Oil Price Assumptions
The cost of crude oil assumed in the 2025 Base tariff determination
was US$ 76.81 per barrel, translating into US$ 571.53 per metric ton
of Heavy Fuel Oil (HFO).
According to the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries
(OPEC), as of the end of May 2025, the cost of the reference basket
of crudeoil wasUS$ 63.62 per barrel, representing a 17.2% decrease
from February 2025. This translates into a cost of US$ 473.39 per
metric ton of HFO.

3.2.2 Energy Purchases by the UETCL from the Electricity
Generation Power Plants
Electricity demand is expected to grow at an annual rate of
approximately 10.4% in 2025 compared to the energy purchases for
2024. The total energy purchased by UETCL is expected to increase
from 6,622.85 GWh for 2024 to 7,311.6 GWh in 2025. In Q3 2025, the
annualized energy purchases by UETCL are projected to be
7,517.53 GWh, presenting an annualized growth of 13.51%
compared to the energy purchases in 2024.
This growth is attributed to the economy's resilience at the macro
level against global economic pressures arising from geopolitical
tensions and a tighter monetary policy implemented by the Central
Bank, which cushioned the economy from inflationary pressures.
The projected growth in demand is further supported by the growth
in West Nile following its connection to the national grid, the rollout
of the Electricity Access Scale-up Project, increased export
opportunities to Rwanda, Kenya, and Tanzania, and the
commissioning of transmission infrastructure, which will unlock the
suppressed demand across the country.
The projection assumed business will continue as usual, with no
major disruptions from the global economy. This is expected to
support smooth business operations, continued reduction in
inflationary pressures, and growth in the overall economy ranging
between 6.5% and 7% for the next twelve months, as projected by
the Bank of Uganda. The continued growth outlook is supported by
improved agricultural and industrial activity, increased investment,
particularly in the extractive sector, and continued implementation
of government initiatives such as the Parish Development Model
(PDM). The next section presents the expected dispatch from
various generation plants during Tariff Year 2025.

3.2.3 Electricity Demand
The capacity plants along the River Nile are expected to balance
the system's demand and supply in consideration of the regulated
water limits, which have an impact on the expected dispatch from
large hydro power plants, such as Karuma HPP. Dispatch is
expected from the other power plants, considering the respective
PPAs and the seasonal nature of small hydro HPPs, as determined
by the System Operator across the country.
3.2.4 Large Hydro Power Plants
(a) Nalubaale and Kiira Hydro Power Plants (380 MW)
The Authority issued a Licence for the Generation and Sale of
Electricity from the Nalubaale and Kiira Hydropower Complex to
the Uganda Electricity Generation Company Limited (UEGCL) for a
period of three (3) years, effective April 2023.
The Nalubaale and Kiira complex, with an installed capacity of 380
MW, is projected to dispatch an average of 209.2 MW in Q3 2025,
equivalent to 1,832.74 GWh. These dispatch levels are expected to
influence the generation scheduling of other power plants along
the River Nile.
The annualized power purchase costs forNalubaale and KiiraHydro
Power Complex are expected to decrease from USh 78.61 billion in
Q2 2025 to USh 78.12 billion in Q3 2025. This decrease is due to the
appreciation of the Uganda Shilling against the United States Dollar.
(b) Bujagali Hydro Power Plant (250 MW)
In 2025, the Bujagali Hydropower Plant (HPP), operated by Bujagali
Energy Limited (BEL), is projected to generate an average capacity
of 156.68 MW, equivalent to 1,372.50 GWh. This generation results
from the Directorate of Water Resources Management limiting
water releases from the Kiira and Nalubaale Hydropower Complex

Based on the projected average dispatch, in Q3 2025, Isimba HPP

According to the Licence for Isimba, the Plant is contracted at an

The power purchase costs for the Isimba Hydro Power Plant are
expected to decrease from USh 186.25 billion in Q2 2025 to USh
174.9 billion in Q3 2025. The projected decrease in Q3 2025 is due
to the appreciation of the Uganda Shilling against the United States
Dollar and decreased dispatch.
(d) Karuma Hydro Power Plant (600 MW)
In Q3 2025, the Karuma Hydropower Plant, operated by the UEGCL,
is projected to generate at an average capacity of 111.1 MWh. This
translates into an annualized energy output of 972.86 GWh,
compared to 1,074.9 GWh in Q2 2025. The reduction reflects
seasonal variations in hydrological conditions and dispatch
priorities within the national grid.
According to the Licence for Karuma, the Plant is contracted at an
energy charge of US cents 4.97 per kWh for the first ten years of the
project. The tariff is adjusted for the US PPI. The adjusted tariff for the
Tariff Year 2025 is US cents 4.981/kWh.
